title: A constructible stratification transfers across etale-local module isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Work with sheaves of $A_X$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], where $A_X$ is the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $F,G$ be such sheaves and let $(i_\alpha:Z_\alpha\hookrightarrow X)_{\alpha<m}$ be a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] witnessing constructibility of $G$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]: its strata are constructible locally closed subsets and each module inverse image $i_\alpha^{-1}G$ is etale locally a constant finite $A$-module sheaf. Suppose there is a jointly surjective etale covering family $\{u_j:U_j\to X\}_{j\in J}$, with no finiteness assumption on $J$, and module-sheaf isomorphisms $u_j^{-1}F\cong u_j^{-1}G$ for every $j$; inverse images use [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then the same stratification witnesses constructibility of $F$: for every $\alpha$, the sheaf $i_\alpha^{-1}F$ is etale locally a constant finite $A$-module sheaf. No compatibility among the local isomorphisms on overlaps is required.

source.place: Tag 03RU, definition-finite-locally-constant, module-sheaf clause; its cover-refinement consequence on a fixed constructible stratification

proof.text: Fix a stratum $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ of the given stratification. By its assumed witnessing property, clause (b) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] gives an etale covering $(v_b:V_b\to Z)_{b\in B}$ and finite $A$-modules $M_b$ with isomorphisms of $A_{V_b}$-module sheaves $\psi^0_b:(i^{-1}G)|_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_b}_{V_b}$, where $|_{V_b}$ is restriction along the functor $(V_b)_{\Et}\to Z_{\Et}$, $(V'\to V_b)\mapsto(V'\to V_b\xrightarrow{v_b}Z)$. Since $v_b$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) gives an isomorphism of abelian sheaves $\rho_b:v_b^{-1}i^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}(i^{-1}G)|_{V_b}$, natural in the abelian sheaf. It is $A$-linear: for $\lambda\in A$, naturality applied to the endomorphism $\lambda\cdot$ of $i^{-1}G$ says that $\rho_b$ intertwines $v_b^{-1}(\lambda\cdot)$, which is multiplication by $\lambda$ for the module structure of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2) (the inverse image of the action map is the action map, and the constant section $\lambda$ of $A_Z$ goes to the constant section $\lambda$ of $A_{V_b}$ under the ring identification (1)), with $(\lambda\cdot)|_{V_b}$, multiplication by $\lambda$ on the restricted module. The local sections $a$ of $A_{V_b}$ with $\rho_b(ax)=a\rho_b(x)$ for all $x$ form a subsheaf of rings containing the constant sections, hence all of $A_{V_b}$, the sheafification of the constant presheaf. Put $\psi_b=\psi^0_b\circ\rho_b:v_b^{-1}i^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{M_b}_{V_b}$, an isomorphism of $A_{V_b}$-module sheaves. This applies the given witness; no new stratification is chosen.

source.place: Tag 03RU, definition-finite-locally-constant (restriction F|_{U_i} to the covering members); Section Tag 03S2, paragraph after Definition Tag 03S3 (definition-extension-zero, part (3) for sheaves of Lambda-modules): 'j^{-1} is just the restriction via the functor U_etale -> X_etale'

proof.text: For each $b$, base change the covering $(u_j:U_j\to X)_{j\in J}$ along $i\circ v_b:V_b\to X$. Write $W_{bj}=V_b\times_XU_j$, with projections $q_{bj}:W_{bj}\to V_b$ and $r_{bj}:W_{bj}\to U_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], $(q_{bj})_j$ is an etale covering of $V_b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition], the family $h_{bj}=v_b\circ q_{bj}:W_{bj}\to Z$ is an etale covering of $Z$. These results allow arbitrary indexing sets, so no quasi-compactness or finite subcover is needed.

Let $\phi_j:u_j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}u_j^{-1}G$ be the supplied isomorphism. All inverse images are module functors by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The equality $i\circ h_{bj}=u_j\circ r_{bj}$ and the module-linear composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear-core] give the following chain, where the middle arrow is $r_{bj}^{-1}\phi_j$ and the penultimate arrow is the inverse image of the trivialization from step 1:
$$h_{bj}^{-1}i^{-1}F\cong r_{bj}^{-1}u_j^{-1}F\cong r_{bj}^{-1}u_j^{-1}G\cong q_{bj}^{-1}v_b^{-1}i^{-1}G\cong q_{bj}^{-1}\underline{M_b}_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_b}_{W_{bj}}.$$
The last comparison is [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] with category of values $\mathrm{Mod}_A$; it preserves the very same finite module $M_b$. Mapping an isomorphism by a functor is elementary: map its inverse and apply the two functor laws. Thus every arrow in the displayed chain is an isomorphism of $A$-module sheaves, not merely of underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; constant-sheaf inverse image also as in the cited blueprint lemma

proof.text: The family $(h_{bj}:W_{bj}\to Z)_{b,j}$ is an etale covering by step 2. Each $h_{bj}$ is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), made $A$-linear by the same argument as in step 1, gives an isomorphism of $A_{W_{bj}}$-module sheaves $(i^{-1}F)|_{W_{bj}}\cong h_{bj}^{-1}i^{-1}F$, and composing with the chain of step 3 gives $(i^{-1}F)|_{W_{bj}}\cong\underline{M_b}_{W_{bj}}$, restriction being along $(W_{bj})_{\Et}\to Z_{\Et}$. Hence the covering $(h_{bj})_{b,j}$ and the finite modules $M_b$ witness clause (b) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] for $i^{-1}F$. Repeat for every one of the finitely many given strata. Their immersions, partition, local closedness and constructibility as subsets have not changed, so clause (a) and all stratification conditions remain satisfied. This proves constructibility of $F$ with the same stratification. Each trivialization was obtained separately on one $W_{bj}$; the definition asks for their existence and imposes no overlap equation. Empty strata are vacuous, and no size bound on either covering family has been introduced.
